title: xdrip+ not synchronising all glucose data points from Nightscout when the measurement insert rate is > 1/5 minutes (libre)
body:
Two setups:
1) Using glimp as an NFC scanner and uploader from a Libre 1 sensor, inserting to Nightscout (14.0.6)
2) Using glimp + Miao Miao as an uploader from a Libre 1 sensor, inserting to Nightscout.

Xdrip+ (current master branch, as of 13/11/2020) was set to act as a Nightscout follower for a primary data source.

The issue that I saw was that I had missing data points in the BG graph - so in case 1) I would scan after a couple of hours, and I would have good recent data, but also a big gap since I had last scanned.

In case 1), looking at what happened more closely, I noted that glimp would upload all of the readings from the Libre.  This meant ~ 15 readings one minute apart, followed by readings every 15 minutes from the older data.

In case 2), I noted that glimp was doing readings 1/minute - I would assume from the behaviour that it is reading every 5 minutes, and getting data by the minute.  This tallies with what I see on the Nightscout website.

Looking through the code, I noted the following in app/src/main/java/com/eveningoutpost/dexdrip/cgm/nsfollow/NightscoutFollow.java:

In function 'work', it uses the MissedReadingsEstimator to estimate a count of missed readings, which it then passes as count parameter on the REST query to limit the number of results returned.

The line is:
int count = Math.min(MissedReadingsEstimator.estimate() + 1, (int) (Constants.DAY_IN_MS / DEXCOM_PERIOD));

This is then followed by another line that ensures that you get at least 10 readings:
count = Math.max(10, count);

In app/src/main/java/com/eveningoutpost/dexdrip/evaluators/MissedReadingsEstimator.java it appears to estimate missed readings as being the number of 5 minutely readings that would fit within the time period since the last BG reading.

(I am not particularly familiar with javascript BTW - so this is the best I could make of it).

So - it looks to me like this method of estimating missed readings and using this count to limit the web query is probably the source of the behaviour.

I tried an experiment, and modified the value to 23 (This is roughly where 15 x 1 minute updates + 1 update / 15 minutes crosses over with a flat 1 update / 5 minutes).
count = Math.max(23, count);

I noted that the synchronisation didn't have gaps in case 1), under the specific conditions that xdrip was syncing more often than the Libra was being scanned.

In case 2) however, I still see gaps if I sync after a while (say, an hour) - which would be consistent with the behaviour above, as I can see on the Nightscount website that the data is being inserted once per minute (Increasing the minimum count is really just band-aiding the issue for some specific usage patterns).

One thing I haven't tried yet is to modify the query to be date-based - for example, something like:
https://your.nightscout.site/api/v1/entries?find[date][$gte]=1605904430000@count=<pick a large value for count>

There are also a couple of potential implications I was wondering about though:
* This will increase the number of results returned, at least under this scenario.  How does this affect Heroku resource limits?  Any potential issues with increased handset data?
* How does this affect local DB storage on the handset?
* Is there any variation in the Nightscout API, where this might not work with older versions?
* Would it potentially run into server-imposed limits on counts in the future?  (Requiring multiple requests if not enough data is returned).

comments.body: The problem is caused by the `MissedReadingsEstimator` which assumes one reading every five minutes (`DEXCOM_PERIOD`).

What is the status of this?

The only caveat I found is that after a number of months, it did get less responsive (At which point I cleared data for the app, and this issue went away).  That said, I don't know if it would have become less responsive anyway.

I've attached some diffs of my changes - I can't regression test though (with the original scenario), as we've since moved from libre to dexcom to get pump integration.

@jeremystringer Is this not related to the following?
https://github.com/NightscoutFoundation/xDrip/issues/929

> @jeremystringer Is this not related to the following?
> #929

I don't believe so, at least looking at the behaviour and the proposed fix for #929.  #929 appears to be about delays getting data from system to system accumulating, causing data not to be available for a while on a follower handset (Complicated, perhaps, by lack of time synchronisation).

This is different - this is essentially that with a libre + glimp as an uploader, more data than expected (> 1 point / 5 minutes) gets inserted into nightscout from the master handset, and the follower handset (with xdrip+) doesn't query enough data to build a full graph, as it bases how much data to query on an estimate of 1 point / 5 minutes.

One big difference with libre + glimp as an uploader is that with the libre you get 15 minutes worth of 1 minute values each time you read (1 point / 1 minute) + historical data (15 minutely, from memory).  Glimp just uploads it all (or did when I raised the bug, at least)

1. Libre v3 Uploads glocose every minute to Nightscout
2. XDrip uses nighscout follower source.

My setup is correct and all data is seen in history. [Image attached] Though on the main screen same data is not available, only some of it. I can see only last 6 hours, which is 1/4 of all data.

Or just a setting under display settings would be fine too where we could manually enter how many num_values we want.

The problem does not only affect the output in xDrip+, but, as the images of the clocks show, also the display on end devices that rely on the web service.
Especially with Garmin watches, the problem is that the amount of the query is very limited to 8 kb, but also the background process itself by which the data is processed is not much larger. Therefore, no more than 24 values should be queried (count=24) to be on the safe side.
Therefore, it is not a solution to query more data and evaluate only every 5th value.
The web service should therefore provide a way to output only one value every 5 minutes.
My watchfaces uses the following query:
http://127.0.0.1:17580/sgv.json?brief_mode=Y&count=24&all_data=Y

The issue is mostly because of the bug in the nightscout follower code which allows records to be stored at a higher frequency than the collector would typically allow. 

I think the best way to address this is a de-duplicator in BgReading which I will work on.

Regarding the watchfaces which use the xDrip web service and are experiencing this problem, please try the Aug 1st nightly which includes de-duplication to the expected 5 minute window when the `brief_mode` parameter is set. Please let me know if this resolves that problem.
